answer: A river survey hires agents to map shale with a spiral-scanning probe. Pay at most one epoch reward per certified probe, using its hardware public key as a spent nullifier; require a fresh nonce signed inside the probe's secure element. Renaming the agent cannot reset that limit. To earn as 100 identities, an attacker needs 100 genuine probes and their operating costs. This depends on one certificate per device and nonexportable keys; software-only checks cannot prove hardware uniqueness.
